title: The Snipe and the Clam
text:
The state of Zhao was preparing to attack its neighbor Yan. The adviser Su Dai traveled to the court of Zhao and told King Huiwen a story.

On the way here, he said, as I crossed the Yi River, I saw a clam lying open on the bank, sunning itself. A snipe came along and pecked at its flesh. The clam snapped its shell shut and caught the bird's beak.

The snipe said: if it does not rain today, and does not rain tomorrow, there will be a dead clam. The clam answered: if I do not let you out today, and do not let you out tomorrow, there will be a dead snipe. Neither would give way. Then a fisherman came along and took them both.

Now, Su Dai said, Zhao is about to attack Yan. If the two states wear each other down in a long war, I fear that powerful Qin will be the fisherman. He asked the king to think carefully.

King Huiwen agreed that he was right, and called off the attack.
lesson: Before locking yourself into a fight with a rival, look around for the third party who gains when you both exhaust yourselves.
people: Su Dai, King Huiwen of Zhao
location: States of Zhao and Yan, Ancient China
source: Zhanguo Ce (Strategies of the Warring States), Yan section
